author: John T. Morse Jr.
claims: The Second Inaugural Address was delivered by Abraham Lincoln.
The address was given at Lincoln's second appearance to take the presidential oath.
Lincoln's anxiety before his first inauguration was about the South forcing a civil war, while his anxiety before his second was about the North dealing too harshly with a conquered South.
The address noted that four years prior, all thoughts were directed to an impending civil war, which both parties dreaded and sought to avert.
The Civil War was caused by the institution of slavery, which was localized in the southern part of the Union.
The insurgents' object was to strengthen, perpetuate, and extend slavery, while the government claimed no right to do more than restrict its territorial enlargement.
Neither party expected the war's magnitude or duration, nor that the cause of the conflict might cease before the conflict itself.
Lincoln suggested that American slavery might be an offense that God willed to remove, and the war was the due woe for those by whom the offense came.

The address expressed a hope that the war would speedily pass away, but acknowledged that if God willed it to continue, it would be until the wealth of the bondman's toil was sunk and blood drawn with the lash was paid by blood drawn with the sword.
The speech concluded with a call to strive to finish the work, bind up the nation's wounds, care for those affected by the war, and achieve a just and lasting peace.
Lincoln believed the speech would wear well, perhaps better than anything else he had produced, but was not immediately popular because it showed a difference of purpose between the Almighty and men.
Lincoln felt the truth that the war was a divine judgment needed to be told, and since the humiliation fell most directly on himself, he thought others could afford for him to tell it.
The speech has been compared to the lofty portions of the Old Testament and is considered one of the most famous written or spoken compositions in the English language.
Lincoln returned to the White House after delivering the address with less than five weeks of life remaining.
